Abstract not available for JP7255812 – the wording below is the version translated from the Japanese, original publication

[0001] The present invention relates to a rolling bearing in which rolling elements in the form of balls move between two bearing races.

[0002] Slewing bearings used as structural components of machine parts are known. Rotational bearing designs vary, but all include a rotating element that moves between two bearing races. Additional components of the rolling bearing may include separators (cages) that maintain the rolling elements at a fixed mutual distance, sealing elements, and the like.

[0003] Slewing bearings provide rotary motion of the shaft, maintain a constant position of its axis of rotation, and also transmit loads, so they have low resistance to motion, stable operation, reliable operation, wear resistance, or It should be characterized by high durability. To achieve minimal energy loss due to friction and reduced noise due to vibration of mating components, bearing races of structural components that mate with rolling elements are ground and then finished. However, slight differences in the dimensions of the rolling elements pose significant problems. Mass-produced rolling elements are sorted in terms of their size, but in practice it is impossible to achieve absolute dimensional uniformity of rolling elements. For example, balls differing in diameter by up to 2 μm are inserted into ball bearings. With a bearing so assembled, for example, at a speed of 1000 rpm, individual balls traveling on the race may cover distances that differ by even 20 mm during one minute of operation. Uneven loading of the rolling elements of the bearing causes further differences in the distance covered by the rolling elements. In rolling bearings that transmit only lateral loads, rolling elements that do not carry loads move to even out the distance covered. In a bearing where all rolling elements are loaded, the spin of the rolling elements relative to the bearing races equalizes the distance covered by the rolling elements. For spin to occur, the ball's force acting on the cage or adjacent balls must increase to a value that exceeds the sliding friction force. The higher the load on the bearing, the greater the sliding friction force. In such cases, the grease used to grease the rolling bearing is a necessary factor to ensure proper fit. Lack of proper greasing is a major contributor to bearing wear. Slewing bearings that have cages made of materials with low coefficients of friction and that transmit only lateral loads can function without greasing.

[0004] International Patent Application No. 2011105919 discloses a bearing consisting of two rings with bearing races, in which a loaded rolling element moves, towards the direction of movement of the rolling element, at least one laterally disposed groove or recess is located in one of the bearing races. A lateral groove or recess may cause the rolling element to momentarily disengage from one of the bearing races and due to the different diameters of the rolling element and uneven loading of the rolling element of the bearing, cage forces or adjacent rolling. Can move under the influence of elemental forces. The lack of slippage between the rolling elements and the races resulting from the use of bearings according to the invention with lateral unfilled grooves or recesses allows operation of the bearings without greasing.

[0005] Bearings with grooves, in particular transverse grooves, or indentations or recesses in the bearing race are disclosed in the following patent specifications: EP 375 938, US 20080285903 ), US Pat.
